Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I’m putting the proposed amendment in writing so your procurement and CloudOps teams can review. High level: we recommend increasing your Reserved Dedicated pool to add 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved), and updating the autoscale policy to meet the throughput guarantees you requested for Q1 ramp.

Summary (proposed) — attached PDF: Acme_Dedicated_Amendment_2026_v1.pdf
- Reserved capacity: +8 A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool)
- Autoscale policy: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=16, warm_pool_size=4
- Scale-up lag target: 30s from request to ready (measured median)
- Throughput guarantee: 3,000,000 tokens/day baseline (billing credit if below SLA)
- Term: 12 months from renewal date; pricing: incremental $14,500/month for reserved uplift (pro-rate on effective date)

Next steps: can you confirm whether procurement needs a 30-day review timeline? If CloudOps prefers a more conservative min_replicas or smaller warm pool we can propose a staged rollout (start with min_replicas=1, warm_pool=2 for first 60 days, then move to 2/4). I’ve attached the initial amendment for redlines.

If this looks directionally correct I’ll loop in Grace (solutions) to propose the technical runbook and a canary plan.

— Marcus

Thanks, Sarah — good questions. Quick answers and an adjusted commercial option attached (Acme_Dedicated_Amendment_2026_v2.pdf).

- Why +8 GPUs: your pilot traffic (sample window) showed sustained tails during business hours that would push a 4x pool above 85% utilization at p95, increasing token latency and error risk. The +8 proposal gives ~2.0x headroom for peak windows; we can model a phased approach (4 -> 8) if procurement prefers.
- p95 latency: based on our test harness run against a copy of your prompt distribution, expected p95 generation latency is ~420ms with warm cache hits; cold-start p95 is higher — see Grace’s benchmark notes below.
- Cache behavior: when an instance is in the warm pool it retains KV cache for the last N tokens and the session store; warm pool instances reduce cold-start token cost by ~70–90% depending on prompt reuse.
- Ramp option: attached v2 includes a 3-step ramp (4 reserved for 45 days, then +4 reserved for 30 days, then full 8 reserved), with automated monitoring gates (throughput and error rate thresholds).

If that tradeoff works we’ll prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment and the SLA addendum. I’ve CC’d Grace to provide the technical runbook for the canary and warm-pool sizing.

— Marcus

Hi all —

I ran the workload profile through our internal benchmark suite against an A100-equivalent baseline. Key observations and recommended autoscale tuning below (long but actionable):

Benchmark highlights (attached: benchmark-results-acme.csv)
- Median cold-start (new replica, no KV cache): ~18s (single-token warm-up plus model load/RT overhead)
- Median warm-start (warm pool instance with KV cache present): ~2.5s
- p95 warm-start: ~6.8s
- Token throughput per A100-eq instance: ~420K tokens/hour with your prompt mix (cached-heavy)

Recommended autoscale policy (conservative -> aggressive):
- Phase 0 (canary, first 14 days): min_replicas=1, warm_pool_size=2, max_replicas=12, scale_up_lag_target=45s (validate traffic patterns)
- Phase 1 (post-canary): min_replicas=2, warm_pool_size=4, max_replicas=16, scale_up_lag_target=30s
- Phase 2 (peak headroom): max_replicas=20 (only enabled by ops override or automated time-based windows)

Notes on warm pool: warm_pool instances keep model weights and the most recent KV pages in memory; we reserve ~8–12GB of GPU memory for the cache on each instance for your workload. That’s why warm_pool_size=4 materially reduces p95.

Runbook (high level)
- Canary traffic routing: 10% of production routed to new pool for first 48 hours; monitor error_rate, p95 latency, and token drop rate.
- Auto-fallback: if p95 exceeds 900ms or error_rate > 0.5% for 10m, automatically route to hosted fallback model for degraded QA and open an Ops incident.

We can implement pre-warming windows (cron) for known business hours to keep warm_pool at target during 8am–6pm PST.

Happy to run a quick 4-hour canary on a day/time that works for your CloudOps team.

— Grace
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
